Oṃ, salutations to Kulavāgīśvarī.

Oṃ. I perpetually bow to Vāgīśvarī, the family preceptor—the Goddess who dwells in the Kadamba forest, who resides within a reddish triangular mandala, who is white and seated upon the pericarp of a white, excellent lotus, and whose lotus-hands are endowed with a fine book and a rosary.
I bow to Tripurāmbā, the Śakti of Śaṅkara, who sketches the wondrous picture of the universe even without a sketching tool, and who bestows all spiritual perfections.
*Hrīṃ vāgīśāya vidmahe klīṃ kāmeśāya dhīṃ sauḥ tannaḥ śaktiḥ pracodayāt*. Having recited this *Gāyatrī* three times.
With "Oṃ hrīṃ phaṭ," place the weapon-vessel (astrapātra) to one's right; with it, perform the sprinkling of all substances.

Having offered a flower upon the seat with "Aiṃ, O foot of the Trikoṇapīṭha," and having sat there, one should perform the rites of breath control (prāṇāyāma) and so forth; then, from one's own self-identification, follows the placement of the twelve kalās.
Oṃ aiṃ hṛ | Oṃ klīṃ śi | Oṃ sauḥ śi | Oṃ aiṃ kṛ | Oṃ klīṃ ne | Oṃ sauḥ astrāḥ ||

Aiṃ, the feet of Aiśānyambā [are placed] in the heart. Aiṃ, the feet of Vāmāmbā in the Kuṇḍalinī. Aiṃ, the feet of Ambāmbā in the abode of the life-force (jīva). Thus is the fivefold division of the Vāgbhava-kalā.

*Klīṃ*, the feet of Vaindavī Ambā, at the location of the *bindu*; *klīṃ*, the feet of Mohinī Ambā, between the eyebrows; *klīṃ*, the feet of Aindrī Ambā, in the heart; *klīṃ*, the feet of Kāmā Ambā, in the secret place. Thus is the *nyāsa* of the *Kāmakalās*. *Sauḥ*, the feet of Visargakalā Ambā, on the head; *sauḥ*, the feet of Triśūlakalā Ambā, in the three channels (*nāḍīs*); *sauḥ*, the feet of Sañjīvanakalā Ambā, in the abode of the life-force (*jīvadhāman*). Thus is the *nyāsa* of the three *Śaktikalās*.
Hrīṃ Phaṭ: illumination of the hands and body, purification of the body, and the production of a new body; the placement of the Vāgbhava-kalā at the base, middle, and tips of the fingers.

The placement of these seed-syllables (*bīja*) is in the anus, the navel, and the cavity of the heart. With *klīṃ phaṭ*, there is the binding of the directions; with *hūṃ*, the veiling. Thus is the rite of immortalization (*amṛtīkaraṇa*).

Then, preceded by breath control (*prāṇāyāma*), having attained a divine body through meditative concentrations (*dhāraṇā*) such as drying [the elements] and so forth, and through the dissolution of the collection of sense organs, one should worship with the most excellent mental offerings after having meditated upon the Goddess— whose form is unmanifest, whose nature is sound (*nāda*), who is gross, holding a book and a rosary, adorned with a garland of *kadamba* flowers, and emitting the Mother-letters (*mātṛkā*). Having thus performed the mental sacrifice (*manoyāga*), one should wash the vessel with the three employed seed-syllables (*bīja*).

Having consecrated [the vessel] with substances appropriate to its own kind, one should fill it; there, one should worship according to the sequence of three or five [deities]. Then, having performed the self-worship (*svātmapūjā*), one should carry out the external sacrifice (*bāhyayāga*).

Aiṃ Hrīṃ, the feet of Lord Kāmadeva; Aiṃ Hrīṃ, the feet of Mother Rati; Oṃ, the feet of Lord Vasanta; Oṃ, the feet of Mother Prīti; Oṃ, the feet of Lord Udyāna. Having worshipped [these] in the left, right, and middle of the door, one should utter the Vāgbhava seed-syllable.
Aiṃ, at the feet of the Guru-Nātha Tripuravāgīśa; Klīṃ, at the feet of the Paramaguru-Nātha Tripurasundara; Sauḥ, at the feet of the Paramācārya-Guru-Nātha Tripuravīra.
Thus, in the triad of gurus, [the mantra] is to be worshipped to the south of the sky (Vyoma): Aiṃ, O feet of Ṣaṣṭheśanātha; Klīṃ, O feet of Mitreśanātha;
Sauḥ, O feet of Uḍḍīśanātha.
Thus ends the triad of Siddhas in Vyomavāmā. Now, in the western part of Vyoma: Aiṃ Hrīṃ, the feet of Ambā Kāmeśvarī; Aiṃ Hrīṃ, the feet of Ambā Sumanādevī; Aiṃ Hrīṃ, the feet of Ambā Saubhāgyadevī;
Aiṃ Hrīṃ, the feet of Ambā Ānandādevī; Aiṃ Hrīṃ, the feet of Ambā Manmathādevī; Aiṃ Hrīṃ, the feet of Ambā Pradyumnādevī; Aiṃ Hrīṃ...

Mahādevanāthapāda | Aiṃ Hrīṃ Anaṅgādevanāthapāda | Aiṃ Hrīṃ Vāmadevanāthapāda | Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śaṅkarānandanāthapāda | Aiṃ Hrīṃ Sāmbhavajñānānandanāthapāda | Aiṃ Hrīṃ Suguptānandanāthapāda | Aiṃ Hrīṃ Musvalānandanātha | Aiṃ Hrīṃ Sugurunātha.
Thus the successions of Siddhas and Mānavas are established.
Then, one should worship the eight Mothers outside.

Aiṃ Hrīṃ, at the feet of Mother Brāhmī; Oṃ, at the feet of Mother Māheśvarī; Oṃ, at the feet of Mother Kaumāri; Oṃ, at the feet of Mother Vaiṣṇavī; Oṃ, at the feet of Mother Vārāhī; Oṃ, at the feet of Mother Aindrī; Oṃ, at the feet of Mother Aiśānī; Oṃ, at the feet of Mother Āgneyī.
Thus, they are to be worshipped starting from one's own front, proceeding in a counter-clockwise direction.
Aiṃ, foot of the Trikoṇa-pīṭha; Aiṃ, foot of the Ambuja-pīṭha; Aiṃ, foot of the Karṇikāgra-pīṭha; Aiṃ, foot of the Kambalagola-pīṭha.

Having thus worshipped within the three petals of the seat, one should contemplate the Goddess— whose form is unmanifest, shaped like a *kadamba* bud, subtle, and consisting of sound; who is gross, holding a book and a rosary in her hands, adorned with a garland of *kadamba* flowers, and emitting the *mātṛkā* letters—
and worship her in the center of the *kadamba* upon a pure, stainless [seat].
Then the root [mantra].
Aiṃ Klīṃ Sauḥ, O feet of the Mother Kulavāgīśvarī; thus is the root mantra.

In a three-cornered, three-layered, three-petaled lotus, the sequence of the three and five should be worshipped in each of the three petals— in the east, south, and left— as well as in the pericarp and above, across these five locations.
Aiṃ, the foot of the Liṅga facing west; Klīṃ, the foot of Ambā in the Yoni-mudrā; Sauḥ, the foot of the seat of the three streams. In the east.

Aiṃ, the foot of the Heart-Self-Arisen Liṅga; Klīṃ, the foot of Mother Kṣobhiṇī Mudrā; Sauḥ, the foot of the Uḍḍiyāna Pīṭha. On the right: Aiṃ, the foot of the Bindu-Bāṇa Liṅga; Klīṃ, the foot of Mother Drāviṇī Mudrā;
Sauḥ, the foot of the Pūrṇagiri Pīṭha. On the left: Aiṃ, the foot of the Itara-Liṅga-Pīṭha; Klīṃ, the foot of Mother Sarvāṅgāsundarī Mudrā.
Sauḥ, the foot of the Kāmarūpa-pīṭha; Aiṃ, the foot of the Akulākāśa-liṅga; Klīṃ, the foot of the Nirālambāmudrā-ambā; Sauḥ, the foot of the Jālandhara-pīṭha.
Thus, upon the pericarp; in this manner, one should worship according to the sequence of three fives.

Having offered the water for the feet (*pādya*) and other items from the *argha* vessel used for the weapons, and having presented the food offerings (*naivedya*) consisting of various kinds of edible foods (*bhakṣya-bhojya*) which have been sprinkled with water, one should meditate on the Goddess as being satisfied,
form the *amṛta-mudrā*, and perform the recitation (*japa*).

The offering (bali) to the Vaṭukas and Yoginīs: *Oṃ aiṃ īṃ klīṃ blūṃ saḥ saḥ samayāmbāpāda*. Having thus recited [the mantra] for Samayā and having bound the Nirālamba-mudrā, one should dismiss the Goddess into her own abode.
Thus concludes the worship of Kulavāgīśvarī.
Now follows the worship of Durgā.
Oṃ hrīṃ duṃ, obeisance to the lion throne. Oṃ hrīṃ duṃ, obeisance to the lotus seat. Oṃ hrīṃ duṃ, obeisance to the form of Durgā. Thus is the mantra of the form.

Having performed the worship of one's own self preceded by the placement (*nyāsa*) of the mantras along with their ancillaries (*sāṅga*), I bow to Durgā—who holds a conch, a bow, and arrows in her hands; who has three eyes; whose crown shines with the rays of the crescent moon; who stands upon a lion; who is praised by asuras and siddhas; who resembles *dūrvā* grass; and who removes misfortune and suffering.
Having meditated thus.
Oṃ hrāṃ hrīṃ duṃ, may Durgā, the remover of all fears, grant happiness; svāhā!
Thus, one should worship with the root mantra.

Then, with the syllable *hrām*, one should offer the limbs (*aṅga*) and present the food offering (*naivedya*), and then perform the dismissal (*visarjana*). *Oṃ hrīṃ duṃ durgāyai namaḥ.* *Oṃ hrīṃ hṛdayāya namaḥ.* *Duṃ śirase svāhā.* *Duḥ śikhāyai vaṣaṭ.* *Gā kavacāya huṃ.* *Namaḥ astrāya phaṭ.*
Now follows the worship of Vanadurgā.
I worship her who resembles a dark rain-cloud, who bears a crescent moon upon her head, who is adorned with a young eye, who moves with a terrifying lion-gait,
whose thick arms carry a conch, a discus, a sword, a shield, a Śārṅga bow, arrows, and a skull-cup, and who has conquered the entire army of the asuras.
Thus ends the section on meditation.

Of this mantra of Śrī Vanadurgā: Araṇyaka is the seer (ṛṣi), Anuṣṭubh is the meter (chandaḥ), and Śrī Vanadurgā is the deity (devatā). The application (viniyoga) is for the sake of attaining one's desired goal.
First, one should perform the ritual placement (nyāsa) with the six limbs and the root mantra.
One should perform self-worship:

Oṃ hrīṃ duṃ, obeisance to Icchāśakti (the Power of Will). Oṃ hrīṃ duṃ, obeisance to Jñānaśakti (the Power of Knowledge). Oṃ, obeisance to Kriyāśakti (the Power of Action). Oṃ, obeisance to Kāminī. Oṃ, obeisance to Kātyāyanī. Oṃ, obeisance to Ratipriyā. Oṃ, obeisance to Ānandā. Oṃ, obeisance to Manonmanī.
Thus end the powers of the sacred seats (pīṭha-śaktis).

Oṃ āṃ, obeisance to Prabhā; īṃ, obeisance to Māyā; eṃ, obeisance to Sūkṣmā; aiṃ, obeisance to Viśuddhā; oṃ, obeisance to Nandinī; auṃ, obeisance to Suprabhā; aṃ, obeisance to Jayā; aḥ, obeisance to Sarvasiddhipradā. Thus, or alternatively, the Pīṭha-śaktis are to be worshipped.
Now, the worship of the door (*dvārapūjā*):
Oṃ gāṃ, salutation to Gaṇapati. Vāṃ, to Vaṭuka. Kṣāṃ, to Kṣetrapāla. Śaṃ, to Śaṅkhanidhi. Paṃ, to Padmanidhi. Jmryūṃ, to Jayā. Bhmryūṃ, to Vijayā. Oṃ duṃ, salutation to Dhanurdharā.
Thus ends the worship of the doors. In the center:
Oṃ hrīṃ hūṃ, obeisance to Mahiṣāsura. Oṃ hrīṃ hūṃ, obeisance to Mahāsiṃha.
Above that, one should worship the Blessed Lady with this mantra:
"Arise, O Puruṣī! Why do you sleep? A danger has come upon me; whether it be possible or impossible, O Blessed Lady, pacify that for me, svāhā!
The syllables are thirty-seven.
Arise, O woman of the heart! Why do you sleep? O crest-lock, fear has come upon me. Whether it be possible or impossible, O Blessed One, [act] for me;
pacify it, svāhā! [This is] the six-limbed [mantra].
Now, in the hexagon:
Salutation to Brahmā and Sarasvatī. Salutation to Lakṣmī and Nārāyaṇa. Salutation to Gaurī and Śaṅkara. Thus on the back.
Oṃ hrīṃ duṃ, salutation to the one who terrifies Madhu and Kaiṭabha. Oṃ, salutation to the crusher of the demon Mahiṣāsura. Oṃ, salutation to the destroyer of Sumbha and Niśumbha.

Thus below. Then, on the eight petals, at the bases of the petals: *Oṃ āryāyai namaḥ*; [and] to Durgā, Bhadrā, Bhadrakālī, Ambikā, Kṣemā, Vedagarbhā, and Kṣemaṅkarī. First, on the petals: *namaḥ* to the conch, to the discus, to the sword, to the shield, to the arrow, to the bow, to the trident, and to the skull.
Then, on the tips of the petals are the Mothers.

Oṃ hrīṃ duṃ āṃ, obeisance to Brāhmī; ḷṃ īṃ, to Māheśvarī; ḷṃ ūṃ, to Kaumārī; ḷṃ eṃ, to Vaiṣṇavī; ḷṃ ḹṃ, to Vārāhī; ḷṃ aiṃ, to Aindrī; ḷṃ auṃ, to Cāmuṇḍā; ḷṃ aḥ, obeisance to Mahālakṣmī. Then the world-protectors (lokapālas).

Lūṃ, obeisance to Indra, who holds a vajra in his hand; Rūṃ, obeisance to Agni, who holds a śakti in his hand, and so forth. Oṃ hūṃ, obeisance to Śivadūtī. Oṃ hrīṃ kṣāṃ krāṃ, obeisance to the arrows. Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ duṃ jvale jvāle śūlini, O wielder of the trident, burn, burn! the evil poison, hūṃ phaṭ svāhā!
Thus ends the worship of Vanadurgā.
Now follows the worship of Gaurī.

May she who dwells on the peak of Gaurīśikhara be well-pleased with me—she by whom Paśupati was obtained as her husband through fierce asceticism. We bow to the Goddess, the Blessed One, who stands upon a lion, bearing a trident, a rosary, a lotus-bud, and a water-pot in her right and left hands; she who is graced with two eyes, whose body is bent by high breasts, whose hair is loose and shimmering, and who has the appearance of a sixteen-year-old maiden.
Salutation to the lotus-seat. Salutation to the seat of Gaurī. Oṃ gauṃ, salutation to the form of Gaurī.
Above that: Oṃ hrīṃ saḥ, O Mahāgaurī, beloved of Rudra, svāhā.
Thus is the root mantra.
Gāṃ hṛ, gīṃ śi, gūṃ śi, gaiṃ ka, gauṃ ne, gaḥ a—
these are the limbs (aṅgas).
Sīṃ, salutation to Jñānaśakti; Suṃ, salutation to Kriyāśakti. Then follow the world-protectors (lokapālas) with their mantras as previously stated:
Spheṃ, salutation to Subhagā; Sphiṃ, salutation to Lalitā; Sphuṃ, salutation to Kāpālinī; Spheṃ, salutation to Kāmamālinī; Lūṃ, salutation to Indra, and so forth.
Thus concludes the worship of Gaurī.
Oṃ, homage to Siddhalakṣmī!
The Goddess, white as pure crystal, with five faces and three eyes, endowed with ten arms and adorned all around with jeweled necklaces—
on her right side...
She carries in her ever-granting right hands: 1) a skull-bowl, 2) a smooth trident, 3) a trident with a perfectly polished blade, 4) the essence of essences, and 5) the supreme [attainment]. || 1 ||
On the left side [of the hands], she holds:

1) a skull-topped staff (utkhaṭvāṅga), 2) a hard and formidable axe (kaṭhinavikaṭāṭaṅka), 3) a powerful goad with a noose (ūrjasviṭaṅkapāśa), 4) a book consisting of the essence of the nectar of wisdom (jñānāmṛtarasamaya-pustaka), and 5) the gesture of fearlessness (abhaya).
I bow to Siddhalakṣmī, who is worshipped by the entire world, who holds a lute with her beautiful, auspicious hands, and whose feet rest upon a lotus and a corpse. || 2 ||

I bow to the Goddess who is the first wave of the power of will (*icchā-śakti*), whose current flows within the Asuras, who is contained within the womb [of consciousness], who is manifested in three ways and flashes forth in five; who is perfectly white like crystal, with the hue of pure jasmine and the moon, mounted upon Rudra, endowed with ten arms, and of slender form—*Oṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ*, at the feet of Kulagaṇapati-nātha! *Oṃ*, at the feet of Kula-gaṇapati-valyabhāmbā! *Oṃ*, at the feet of Vaṭukanātha! *Oṃ*.
Vaṭukavalyabhāmbāpāda | Oṃ Gaṅgāmbāpāda | Oṃ Yamunāmbāpāda | Thus is the worship of the door (dvārapūjā).
Now, the lineage of gurus (*gurukrama*):

Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ, the feet of Paramaśivanātha; Oṃ, the feet of Śivanātha; Oṃ, the feet of Ekanettranātha; Oṃ, the feet of Kālāgnirudranātha; Oṃ, the feet of Śrīkaṇṭhanātha; Oṃ, the feet of Pārvatī Ambā; Oṃ, the feet of Daśakaṇṭha (Kandara)nātha; Oṃ...
Dīpikācāryanāthapāda; Oṃ Andhakāsuranāthapāda; Oṃ Jayadrathanāthapāda; Oṃ Caryānandanāthapāda; Oṃ Sundaranāthapāda; Oṃ Gaganabhūtināthapāda; Oṃ Indrabhūtināthapāda; Oṃ Bhāskaranāthapāda;
Oṃ Padmādevyambāpāda; Oṃ Svagurunāthapāda. Thus is the lineage of the gurus.
Now, the worship of the seat (āsana-pūjā):
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, obeisance to Ādhāraśakti; Oṃ, to Ananta; Oṃ, to Dhātrī; Oṃ, to Surārṇava; Oṃ, to Padmāsana; Oṃ Hūṃ, obeisance to Rudrāsana; Oṃ, to Pretāsana.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Aṃ Āṃ Iṃ Īṃ Uṃ Ūṃ Ṛṃ Ṝṃ Ḷṃ Ḹṃ Eṃ Aiṃ Oṃ Auṃ Aṃ Aḥ, obeisance to Kadambavāgīśvarī.

Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Kaṃ Khaṃ Gaṃ Ghaṃ Ṅaṃ, obeisance to Haṃsavāgīśvarī. Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Caṃ Chaṃ Jaṃ Jhaṃ Ñaṃ, obeisance to Citrāvāgīśvarī. Oṃ Ṭaṃ Ṭhaṃ Ḍaṃ Ḍhaṃ Ṇaṃ, obeisance to Medhāvāgīśvarī. Oṃ Taṃ Thaṃ Daṃ Dhaṃ...
Oṃ naṃ, salutation to Vedyāvāgīśvarī. Oṃ paṃ phaṃ baṃ bhaṃ maṃ, salutation to Bhogyāvāgīśvarī.
Oṃ yaṃ raṃ laṃ vaṃ, salutation to Subhagāvāgīśvarī. Oṃ śaṃ ṣaṃ saṃ haṃ, salutation to Gaurīvāgīśvarī.
The eight groups [of syllables] are on the eight petals; above that, with the root-vidyā. There, first of all, one should perform the self-nyāsa according to the sequence to be described:
*Oṃ namaḥ sarvasiddhiyoginībhyaḥ namaḥ | sarvasiddhimātṛbhyaḥ | namo nityoditānandananditāyai sakalakulacakranāyikāyai bhagavatyai caṇḍakāpālinyai*.

It is as follows: Oṃ hrīṃ hrūṃ hāṃ pheṃ kṣoṃ kroṃ namaḥ | Oṃ, O Supreme Haṃsinī, Goddess who bestows the path to Nirvāṇa, pacifier of calamities and misfortunes, crusher of all evils, enemies, and afflictions, ferry across the ocean of all disasters, subduer of all foes, O Goddess, come, come! laugh, laugh! leap, leap!
O consumer of human blood, entrails, and fat! Crush my enemies, crush them! Eat them, eat them! Pierce them with your trident, pierce them! Cut them with your sword, cut them!

Strike them, strike them! Sever them, sever them! Accomplish all my desires until they are fulfilled! O most compassionate Blessed One! O you who assume the form of Mahābhairava! O you who are saluted by the best of the thirty gods! O Mother of all mantras! O Goddess Mahākālī, who are affectionate toward those who bow before you! O destroyer of Time (Kāla)!
Hūṃ hūṃ hūṃ! Make her, who is afflicted by passion, gracious; make her, the maiden of the gods and asuras! Hrīṃ śrīṃ hāṃ hūṃ phaṭ phaṭ phaṭ svāhā!
The syllables are 29; this is the root-vidyā of Siddhalakṣmī.
Now, its method of ritual placement (nyāsa) is written down.

Oṃ, homage to all the Yoginīs of Accomplishment! Homage to the eastern face; one should place [the mantra] on the eastern face. Oṃ, homage to all the Mothers of Accomplishment; homage to the southern face. Homage to her who is ever-arisen and gladdened by bliss; homage to the western face. Homage to the mistress of the entire wheel of families;
homage to the northern face. Homage to the Blessed Lady Caṇḍakāpālinī; homage to the upper face. *Ta* is in the mouth; *dya* is in the heart; *thā* is in the navel.

Oṃ at the mouth; Hrīṃ at the left nostril; Hūṃ at the right nostril; Hāṃ at the left eye; Pheṃ at the right eye; Kṣoṃ at the left ear; Kroṃ at the right ear; Na at the heart; Maḥ at the dvādaśānta (the end of the twelve finger-breadths above the head). This is according to the sequence of the *Muṇḍa* [Tantra].

One should perform the placement [of mantras] (nyāsa) upon the nine gates: *Oṃ paramahaṃsini hṛdayāya namaḥ* (to the heart); *nirvāṇamārgade śiraḥ* (to the head); *viṣamopaplavapraśamani śikhā* (to the crest-lock); *sakalarduritāriṣṭakleśadalani kavaca* (to the armor); *sarvāpadambhodhitaraṇi nettra* (to the eyes); *sakalaśatrupramathini astrā* (to the weapon).
This is the six-limbed placement (*ṣaḍaṅganyāsa*).
With this very weapon-mantra, one should perform the binding of the directions (*digbandhana*) and other rites:
*Oṃ devi āgaccha 2 hasa 2 valga 2 nararudhirāntravasābhakṣiṇikādyāya namaḥ*.
[This is for] the right hand.
One should perform the placement with the *kādyamudrā*: "Mama svaśatrūn marda 2 khāhi 2, obeisance to the khaṭvāṅga"—in the left hand.
"With the trident, bhindi 2, obeisance to the trident"—in the right hand. "Chindi 2 with the sword, obeisance to the sword"—on the right.
Strike, strike! Homage to the noose on the left.
Cut, cut! Homage to the goad on the right.
Do so until you accomplish all my desires! Homage to the boon-granting [hand] on the right.
Homage to the supremely compassionate one, the Fearless, on the left;
homage to the Blessed One who assumes the form of Mahābhairava, on the left; homage to the book, on the left;
homage to the axe revered by the best of the thirty gods, on the left.
Thus ends the assignment of weapons.
"O Mother of all mantras, salutations to Mātṛkā!"— by this [mantra],

one [worships] the Blessed Lady, whose nature is the generation of the phonemic Mātṛkā consisting of the groups *a, ka, ca, ṭa, ta, pa, ya, śa*, and who is the form of the unstruck sound (*anāhatanāda*).
"The nature of Śakti has been revealed"—this is the root [verse].
"Obeisance to Rudrāsana, who is compassionate toward those who bow down. Having thus meditated upon the Bhairava-form vehicle, one should place it within the Blessed Lady.
Then, having performed the invocation: "O Goddess Mahākālī, destroyer of Time (Kāla)."
One should invoke the Blessed Lady with the three *piṇḍas*:

*huṃ huṃ huṃ*. By this, the activity of the Blessed Lady, which destroys time in the form of the five objects of sense, the five senses, the five vital breaths (*prāṇas*), and the grasped, the grasping, and the grasper, is demonstrated.
And that *piṇḍanātha*, which is of the nature of sound (*nāda*), becomes the supreme power (*paramaśakti*) through the *avolyāsikā* [process].

Having meditated upon the form of the Goddess as desired—[reciting] "Oṃ, be gracious; make [her] afflicted with passion for the maidens of gods and asuras"—one should place the syllable *hrīṃ* in the *kanda*.

*Śrīṃ* at the navel; *hūṃ* at the heart; *phaṭ* at the throat; *phaṭ* at the palate; *phaṭ* at the place of the *bindu*; *svā* at the end of sound and non-sound (*nādanādānta*); *hā* at the end of the twelve (*dvādaśānta*).
Thus ends the description of the five faces.

Of that Blessed Lady, the Mother of the three worlds, the ten arms—left and right—are respectively composed of earth, water, fire, air, and ether; they consist of the moon, sun, and fire, and represent the forms of emanation, maintenance, and withdrawal; [and her] ears, skin, and eyes...

The tenfold objects—consisting of the tongue, nose, speech, hands, feet, anus, and genitals, along with their corresponding ten powers (astras) characterized by sound, touch, form, taste, and smell, as well as speaking, grasping, moving, excreting, and experiencing bliss—are thus merged therein. In this way, the Goddess Śakti, being the very covering of the Supreme Śiva whose body is the *kula*, is the manifestation of His absolute freedom (*svātantrya*); pervading all bodies, she is non-different from Him as His attribute (*dharma*) and the possessor of that attribute (*dharmī*).
It proceeds.
May there be auspiciousness!
Oṃ hūṃ, obeisance to the Greatly Worshipful One. Thus is the offering.
Hsvīṃ sphuṭ! O Great Caṇḍa Yoginī! Ṭhstrīṃ sphuṭ! Thstrīṃ sphuṭ! Ṭhstrīṃ sphuṭ! Thus is the *samaya*.
Thus ends the concise ritual manual for the worship of Siddhalakṣmī.
Oṃ, homage to the Blessed Lady Śrī Śārikā.

May the Blessed Goddess Śrī Śārikā, who is endowed with a group of seven, protect us— she who is radiant with seven seed-syllables, whose form possesses the splendor of the sun, whose pair of lotus feet are saluted by the Seven Sages, who removes the suffering of the seven worlds, and who fashioned the cage of the universe as a mere ornament yet released Pradyumna.
Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ gaṇapataye vauṣaṭ | Oṃ gaṇapati-vallabhāyai vauṣaṭ | Oṃ muṇḍarāya vauṣaṭ | Thus are the door-keepers.
Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ I worship the sandals of the Guru-nātha, obeisance. Likewise [I worship] the Siddhas, beginning with the Paramaguru, Parameṣṭhi, and Paramācārya.
The objects of worship: on the left, *oṃ padmāsanāya namaḥ*;
above that—
One should worship the Blessed Lady. Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ hūṃ pheṃ āṃ śāṃ, obeisance to Śārikā. This is the root mantra.
Then the limbs:
ŚRĀṂ HṚD; ŚRĪṂ ŚIRAḤ; ŚRŪṂ ŚIKHĀ; ŚRAIṂ KAVAÇA; ŚRAUṂ NETRA; ŚRAḤ ASTRAṂ.
Now, the ritual placement (*nyāsa*): *Oṃ* on the mouth; *hrīṃ* on the right nostril; *śrīṃ* on the left nostril; *hūṃ* on the right eye; *pheṃ* on the left eye; *āṃ*.

The ritual placement (*nyāsa*) is as follows: *śāṃ* on the right ear; *śā* on the left ear; *ri* on the head; *kā* at the heart; *yai* at the navel; *na* at the *kanda*; *ma* on the thighs. Then: *oṃ hrīṃ aṃ amāyai namaḥ*; *oṃ hrīṃ kaṃ kāmāyai namaḥ*; *oṃ hrīṃ caṃ cārvāṅgyai namaḥ*; *oṃ hrīṃ ṭaṃ*.
Oṃ *ṭāṃ* Tvarāyai namaḥ. Oṃ hrīṃ *taṃ* Tārāyai namaḥ. Oṃ hrīṃ *paṃ* Pārvatyai namaḥ. Oṃ hrīṃ *yaṃ* Yakṣiṇyai namaḥ. Oṃ hrīṃ *ruṃ* Rukmiṇyai. Oṃ hrīṃ *śaṃ* Śambharāyai namaḥ.
Thus it is extracted from the Kalpa.
Oṃ hrīṃ hūṃ kāṃ kāṃ kāṃ—thus is the triad of divisions. Oṃ hrīṃ hūṃ, obeisance to Amāyā; in this manner, the goddesses are to be worshipped. Oṃ hrīṃ jaṃ, obeisance to Jambālajalendra.
Thus [is the mantra] of Kṣetreśa.
Thus concludes the worship of Śārikā.

One should meditate upon the auspicious goddess, who has hands displaying the gestures of granting boons and fearlessness, who holds a sword and a trident, who resembles pure crystal, and who is seated upon a lotus.
Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ phreṃ, obeisance to Ekāntī. This is the root mantra.
The deposition on the body, beginning with the hands, shall occur in a single utterance; thus [is] the solitary one.
Oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ khphreṃ hsrauṃ, salutation to the Blessed One, Kubjikā.
Ṅa ña ṇa name | Aghoramukhi | Krāṃ krīṃ kiṇi kiṇi vicche | Thus [is] Kubjikā.
Oṃ hrīṃ phreṃ śrīṃ Caṇḍayogeśvarī, O Bhavabhavānī, bestower of all desires, giver of all good fortune, hrīṃ namaḥ svāhā.
Thus ends the mantra for the knife (kurikā).

Oṃ! May that goddess of speech, who is endowed with four arms, holding a rosary made of crystal in one hand, and likewise a white lotus, a wine-cup, and a book with another; she who shines with a luster resembling jasmine, the moon, a conch, and crystal, and who is peerless—may she dwell forever, ever well-pleased, within our mouths. Aiṃ vada vada vāgvādini svāhā!
Thus is the root mantra.
*Aiṃ* [to the heart], *vada vada śivāgvā śidini kasvāne* [O Goddess of Speech, speak, speak!], *hāḥ* [to the weapon]. Thus is the worship of Vāgvādinī.
I take refuge in the Vitastā, who holds a rosary, a lotus, a mirror, and a water-pot in her hands, and who sits upon a fish-throne and a lotus-seat.
Oṃ śrīṃ gāṃ gīṃ saḥ, salutation to Vitastā. [The Root Mantra]
*gāṃ hṛ gīṃ śi gūṃ śi gaiṃ ka gauṃ ne gaḥ astrā | hsvyrāṃ gāṃ gīṃ gūṃ gīṃ gaḥ vitastāyai namaḥ |* Thus is another [mantra]. This is the worship of Vitastā.
The meditation on Jvālāmukhī is as follows:
"O Mother, you who have the flames of the fire at the end of the aeon bound in your long hair; you whose face is fierce and beautiful, and who are firm in your vows, O Vaikartanī!"
May we know Ambikā; may we meditate upon Mahāmāyā. May that Mother impel us.
*Ḷ* Oṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Phuṃ, obeisance to the Blessed Jvālā. Oṃ Hrīṃ Hṛ Śrīṃ Śi Phuṃ Śi Jvālā Ka, obeisance to the Blessed One, the Weapon.

Salutation to Gaurī—on the left foot. To Gāyatrī—on the right [foot]. To Sāvitrī—on the left knee. To Sarasvatī—on the right [knee]. To Naralakṣmī—on the navel. To Ubhā—on the left shoulder. To Kāmā—on the right [shoulder]. To Bhavānī—on the head. Salutation to Lakṣmī. To Pū (Pūrṇā)—to the east; to Ma (Māyā)—to Tuṣṭi; to Da (Dakṣā)—to Puṣṭi; to Nai (Nairṛtī)—to Sudhā; to Pa (Pātālī)—to Svāhā; to Vā (Vāruṇī)—to Dhṛti; to U (Uttarā)—salutation to Mati. One should worship [these goddesses] in the directions starting from the east.
In the center: *Oṃ jvālāmukhyai namaḥ*. This is the *mūrti-mantra*. Then one should recite the root mantra (*mūla*) together with its limbs (*sāṅga*).

I bow to Jvālā, the glory of the heart-lotus, who resides upon the mountain of flames; she who has three eyes, who is established upon the three seats, and who is adorned with a profusion of blazing fire; she of beautiful countenance, eternally invisible to worldly mortals; she whose splendor shines with the wonderful variety of supreme majesty; she who is white, the granter of desires, whose feet are worshipped by gods and Siddhas.
Having meditated upon meditation.
Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ (heart) jvālāmukhi, devour (crown) all my enemies, devour (eyes) hūṃ phaṭ (weapon) svāhā. This is the root mantra of Aparajvālā. ||i||
Oṃ, homage to Pūrṇā.
Holding a bow in one hand, an arrow in another, a noose in a third, and a goad in the fourth,
she appeared as a certain radiant goddess whose exceedingly beautiful surface was flowing with bliss.

Red in hue, clad in a garment of human skin, shining like the rays of the new moon, intent on bestowing food, and bowed by the weight of her breasts— she who is adorned with a crescent moon, I am her devotee.
Beholding her delighted, I worship the Blessed Lady, the remover of the suffering of worldly existence.
May we ourselves know food; may we ourselves eat and meditate upon it. May Ambā inspire us in this regard.

*Ḷ* Oṃ, obeisance to the Blessed One, Māheśvarī Annapūrṇā. Oṃ Hrīṃ, obeisance to the Sovereigness Annapūrṇeśvarī. Hrāṃ Hrīṃ Hrūṃ Hraiṃ Hrauṃ Hraḥ are the limbs. Thus concludes the worship of Annapūrṇā.
Oṃ, homage to Lakṣmī.
May Kamalā protect us—she who, seated upon a lotus, her face smiling, holds with her lotus-hands the gestures of generosity, the pair of lotuses, and fearlessness;
she who resembles a flash of lightning in form, shining with a broad and lofty chest adorned with radiant pearls, and who gladdens Hari with the splendor of her side-long glances.

Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ Lakṣmī, Mahālakṣmī, bestower of all desires, giver of all good fortune, grant what is desired! Grant it, grant it! O you who are all-pervading, formless, and the liberator from all suffering! Hrīṃ saḥ svāhā! (The weapon-mantra.)
Thus ends the mantra of Lakṣmīvidyāgavākṣī.

I perpetually worship with supreme devotion Lakṣmī, whose face is red, who holds a lotus and a skull in her hands, who has three eyes, who is intent on her divine play, who is mounted upon the king of elephants, who is bowed to by Brahmā, Indra, and Rudra, and who is served by gods and Siddhas.
Oṃ hūṃ (heart) sarveṣāṃ (head) hastān (arms) mama (thighs) dhanaṃ dehi (feet) hūṃ vittalakṣmyai svāhā. Thus concludes the worship of Vittalakṣmī.
Homage to Haṃsavāgīśvarī!

She who, through the manifestation of the body, arises as the supreme *parā*, *paśyantī*, *madhyamā*, and *vaikharī* speech; she who dwells upon the excellent mountain of Kāśmīra in the form of the Veda; that Vāgīśī, the mother of the worlds—may she protect you. Thus [ends] the Mūlasūtra.

With a single face, arms like lightning, and eyes whose lashes possess the grace of hovering bees, she is joyful; with hands white as jasmine, the moon, a pearl necklace, and a smile, she holds a book and excellent rosary beads.

I bow down with devotion to the Blessed Lady Vāgīśvarī, who is seated upon a lotus throne supported by six lions, who bestows all prosperity, and who is ever-joyful; and in whose heart, in one place, dwells her own form as Haṃsavāgīśvarī with the face of a swan.
Oṃ. To the feet of Gaṇapatīnātha; to the feet of Gaṇapativallabhāmbā; to the feet of Vaṭukanātha; to the feet of Gurunātha; to the feet of Guruvallabhāmbā.

At the doors, the deities of the directions, Nandin, Mahākāla, Gaṅgā, Yamunā, and the threshold (dehalī) are to be worshipped. (Salutation to the deities of the directions; to Nandin, Mahākāla, Gaṅgā, Yamunā, and the threshold.)

Oṃ hrīṃ hsrūṃ aiṃ kraṃ maṃ veḍābhagavati haṃsarūpiṇi svāhā || Hsūṃ, obeisance to Viṣṇu. Oṃ hūṃ hauṃ phaṭ, obeisance to Saṅkara. Obeisance to Jambinī; obeisance to Mohinī, Kāntī, Lakṣmī, Raktā, Śuṣkā, and Utpalā. Thus concludes the worship of Haṃsavāgīśvarī.
Oṃ, homage to the Blessed Queen!

I bow to her whose form is adorned with twelve suns, who sits alone upon a lion-throne and is encircled by serpents; to that Goddess who has attained sovereignty beyond the reach of words, the Queen of Ultimate Reality, whose very body is Bharga.
We know the digit of the Sun; we meditate upon the jewel of light; may that Queen impel us.

Oṃ gāṃ, homage to Gaṇapati! Oṃ, homage to Bhīmarāja! Homage to Kumāra! At the door. Now, for the Nāgas: in the east, homage to Vāsuki; to Nīlanāgarāja (ā); to Takṣaka (da); to Kārkoṭa (nai); to Padmanāga (pa); to Mahāpadma (vā); to Śaṅkhapāla (ta); homage to Kulikanāgarāja (ī). In the center, [homage] to the one adorned with jewels of a thousand rays.

Salutation to the one who possesses a thousand enjoyments, two thousand eyes, and two thousand tongues; who is surrounded by ten million nāgas; who wears yellow garments; who holds a mace in his hand; and who is the king of the infinite nāgas.
On his back:
Salutation to the one seated upon a lotus (*kamalāsanāya namaḥ*).

Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ rāṃ, salutation to the Goddess Rājñī. Oṃ hrīṃ hṛ śrīṃ śi rāṃ, [salutation to] the head; rāṃ śikhā, [salutation to] the crest-lock. Rājñī ka, salutation to the Goddess Bhagavatī as the weapon (*astrā*). Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ rāmaśūrāya kṣettrēśvarāya vauṣaṭ.

Oṃ! I worship the Great Goddess Rājñī, who has the cool-rayed moon and the young sun as her eyes, who possesses four arms, who is seated upon a deer-skin seat, who holds a conch, a lotus, a trident, and a sword, and who is not of the form of a mountain.

Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ rāṃ klīṃ sauḥ, homage to the Blessed Queen, hrīṃ svāhā. Rāṃ rīṃ rūṃ raiṃ rauṃ raḥ are the limbs. Oṃ hrīṃ, homage to Vijayā. Hrāṃ, homage to Jaganmātṛ (Mother of the World). Hrauṃ, homage to Jayā. Hraḥ, homage to Jagaddhātrī (Sustainer of the World).
This was completed on the eleventh day of the bright fortnight of the month of Tapas, in the year one hundred and nineteen, in the sixth cycle, conjoined with fire (three).
May this *Śrīsatpaddhati*, which bestows liberation, composed by Ānandakaula through the grace of the venerable True Guru, be for the pleasure of the illustrious Śambhu. (2)
Now follows the worship of Śāradā.

May this autumnal goddess, seated upon a lion-throne, possessing three eyes, radiant with the luster of gold, and endowed with weapons known as the arrow, the bow, the spear, the bell, the jar of nectar, and the rutting elephant— grant us prosperity and bestow all fruits.

*Grāṃ* to Caṇḍa, *Namaḥ*. *Gūṃ* to Pracaṇḍa, *Namaḥ*. Thus, the two door-keepers. *Oṃ krauṃ gauṃ* to Kālī, *Vauṣaṭ*. *Oṃ śrauṃ* to Mahāgajakālī, *Vauṣaṭ*. *Jrauṃ* to Mahāpadmakālī, *Vauṣaṭ*. *Oṃ trauṃ* to Sarasvatī, *Aiṛphaṭ*. *Oṃ prauṃ* to Śvetacūḍā, *Vauṣaṭ*. *Vrauṃ* to Mahācandrā, *Vauṣaṭ*. *Śrauṃ* to Māhendrī.

Vauṣaṭ! Hrauṃ kāmayair phaṭ! Śrauṃ, salutation to Mahāśaṅkukarṇā! Brauṃ, salutation to Pāṭalā! Lrauṃ, salutation to Vindhyavāsinī! Rmryauṃ, salutation to Mahāpāśāṇḍinī! Oṃ rarmryauṃ, salutation to Mahāśailarūpiṇī! [It is also said: "Pāyai."
Oṃ trauṃ, homage to the one worshipped by the gods for great accomplishment. Oṃ śrīṃ (hrīṃ), phreṃ phaṭ, [homage] to the great all-pervading gurus.
[The crocodile (*kumbhīra*) is said to be the seat of this [deity]; it is explained here because it is not well known.

It has the neck of a camel, the trunk of an elephant, a heart, and ears like those of a boar; its face is like that of a *huḍa* (a type of wild boar); its form resembles the legs of a serpent; its claws are like vajra-weapons; its back is like that of a tortoise, and its tail is like that of a fish—such is the crocodile.]
Thus it is proclaimed: he whose dwelling is like that of a *huḍa* (ram) or a *meṣa* (ram), and whose [claws] are like nails by means of the weapon called the *vajra*.
This is the circle of the Mothers (*mātṛcakra*).
Oṃ, salutation to the lotus seat (*padmāsana*). Oṃ śrīṃ kubhīra hūṃ; this is the form and the seat. The teachers beginning with Āditya. Oṃ śmrīṃ, salutation to Śāradā.

*Sudhā*—this is the root mantra. *Smrīṃ* for the heart (*oṃ*), *śāśi* for the chest (*oṃ*), *dāka* for the head (*oṃ*), *yaine* for the weapon (*oṃ*). *Sudhā* is the weapon. The preceptors are Āditya and the other planets, Viśvakarman, Prabhāsa, Śrīghana, Nandi, and others. *Hrīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ* for the Blessed Lady Śāradā; *hrīṃ śrīṃ saḥ 2 oṃ*.
Salutation to the Blessed Lady Śāradā. Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ khchrīṃ, salutation to the Blessed Lady Śāradā. This is the fourth [mantra].
Oṃ hrīṃ saḥ, salutation to the Blessed Lady Śāradā, hrīṃ svāhā. This is the fifth [mantra].
Thus concludes the worship of Śāradā.
Now, the worship of Jyeṣṭheśvarī:
Oṃ hrīṃ rcrīṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ haḥ phaṭ | Salutation to Jyeṣṭheśvarī. Oṃ hrīṃ jñrīṃ salutation to Yogeśvarī. Thus [ends] Yogeśvarī.
In the center of that, one should worship the goddess named Ekāntī, the presiding deity, who has one face, eight arms, three eyes, and is adorned with ornaments.
Then [he should meditate on] the goddess who resembles a lotus, as red as the rays of the rising sun, holding a skull and a khaṭvāṅga staff, and bestowing the boon with her noose and goad.
Resembling the hibiscus flower, comparable to the pomegranate blossom, resembling a ruby, and like water infused with saffron.
Adorned with a network of tiny bells from the rubies in her shimmering crown, she was beautified by the weight of her braid, fragrant with flowers and sweetly scented.
Her sprout-like curls were as dark as a swarm of bees, and the orb of her lotus-face was like a freshly blossomed, deep red dawn.
I bow to the Supreme Goddess, whose forehead is adorned with a soft fillet curved like a crescent moon, and whose beautiful eyebrows are shaped like the bow of Pināka.
Her eyes were playfully swinging, surging with waves of bliss and joy; her golden earrings were spread wide by the mass of shimmering rays [emanating from them].

Her expansive cheeks were like the full orb of the moon, surpassing its circle of nectar; her nose was clearly defined by the very measuring-line for the creation of Viśvakarman and the other celestial architects.
Her lips, red as copper, coral, or the bimba fruit, were like nectar; she surpassed the ocean of the essence of sweetness with the sweetness of her smile.
Adorned with rows of pomegranate seeds like diamonds, endowed with incomparable qualities, and graced by the region of her chin.
She had a neck like a conch shell and large eyes, and was graced by arms as graceful as lotus stalks, which were adorned with the weight of jeweled bracelets and armlets.
Her form resembles a red lotus, and her delicate lotus-hands possess the radiance of their nails which illuminates the expanse of the sky.
She possessed high breasts adorned with strings of pearls, and her waist was beautifully graced by the curvature of the three folds of skin.
Adorned with a navel whose form was like a whirlpool of loveliness, she possessed hips graced by a girdle fashioned from priceless gems.
The Mistress, whose hips are like two elephant globes, whose line of hair is like a choice goad, and whose thighs are as delicate as the graceful trunk of a plantain tree.
Adorned with a pair of shanks like plantain trees in their loveliness, her two feet possessed hidden ankles, and her foreparts surpassed the tortoise in beauty.
I bow to her whose lotus feet are rubbed by the crest-jewels of the gods, and who is resplendent with moon-like nails shining upon her long toes.
Her splendor resembles a hundred moons, her continuous smile is radiant, and she possesses the crimson hue of the Japā flower and pomegranate, surpassing even the redness of vermilion.
Clad in red garments, with noose and goad raised in her hands, she is seated upon a red lotus and adorned with red ornaments.
She has four arms and three eyes, holds five arrows and a bow, and her mouth is filled with betel-leaf mixed with pieces of camphor.
Her body is intensely red with saffron and abundant musk; she is enriched with all the finery of amorous grace and adorned with every ornament.
She who generates joy for the world, she who causes delight to the world, she who effects the attraction of the world, and she whose form is the cause of the world.
The Goddess who consists of all mantras, beautiful with all auspiciousness, eternally composed of all prosperity, and delighted by supreme bliss.
Having recollected the Mahātripura-mudrā in the form of a vehicle, one should perform obeisance with the Vidyā that is auspicious when mounted and joined with the ritual of salutation.
Having meditated upon Mahātripurasundarī in the center of the wheel according to the previously described method, the best of practitioners should then begin the worship.

One should contemplate [the deity] as being satisfied by pleasant dwellings, beautiful canopies, parasols, chowries, dance, song, recitation, meditative absorption (*samādhi*), fire-offerings (*homa*), and so forth. Then, for the sake of the external sacrifice, one performs the worship of the vessel of water (*arghapātra*) with the primary faces and limbs on one’s own left. [O Goddess,] having worshipped the Gurus to the east of the station of Brahmā, one should worship Vināyaka in the north-west (*vāyavya*) in due order with perfumes and flowers. For the sake of removing obstacles, one should first worship Gaṇapati in the north-west. After that—

In the eastern direction, for the purpose of the sequential order beginning with the Guru, one should bind the *amṛtamudrā* and, having consecrated all the ritual offerings (*upacāra*) with drops of that water, worship oneself as the very nature of Śiva with perfumes, flowers, and so forth. Then, one should perform the *śivahasta*.
Thereafter, the worship of the Gurus should be performed in one's own left, in an upward sequence from bottom to top. Right here, the worship of Śrī Gaṇapati is also performed.

Oṃ gūṃ gāṃ, obeisance to Gaṇapati. Oṃ vāṃ, obeisance to Vāgīśvarī. Thus, in the northwest (vāyu). Oṃ, obeisance to the Guru. Oṃ, obeisance to the Paramaguru. Oṃ, obeisance to the Parameṣṭhiguru. Oṃ, obeisance to the Paramācārya. Oṃ, obeisance to the Ādisiddhas. Oṃ kṣāṃ, obeisance to Kṣetrapāla. Thus, on the left is the lineage of Gurus (gurupaṅkti). On this very occasion, during special days, there is the worship of the water-pot (kalaśapūjana). [I seek] their permission...

Having taken up the worship of the seat: *oṃ anantāya namaḥ* | *oṃ ādhāraśaktaye namaḥ* | *oṃ kandāya namaḥ* | *oṃ aṅkurāya namaḥ* | *oṃ nālāya namaḥ* | *oṃ ṛṃ dharmāya namaḥ* | *oṃ ṝṃ jñānāya nama� sandals* | *ḷṃ vairāgyāya namaḥ* | *ḹṃ aiśvaryāya namaḥ*.
These sandals are white, red, yellow, and black.
From the southeast (Agni) to the northeast (Īśāna), they should be meditated upon as having the form of lions and three eyes, and they are to be worshipped.
*Oṃ*, obeisance to Adharma; *oṃ*, obeisance to Ignorance (*ajñāna*); *oṃ*, obeisance to Non-detachment (*avairāgya*); *oṃ*, obeisance to Lack of Sovereignty (*anaiśvarya*).
These limbs are white in color and take the form of lion-throne pedestals.

From the east to the north: *Oṃ* salutation to the Ṛgveda; *Oṃ* salutation to the Yajurveda; *Oṃ* salutation to the Sāmaveda; *Oṃ* salutation to the Atharvaveda. Having meditated upon this quartet of Vedas as being in the form of the two sandals of the limbs together with the central pivot, one should perform the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) and worship them.

Oṃ, salutation to the Kṛta Yuga; salutation to the Tretā Yuga; salutation to the Dvāpara Yuga; Oṃ, salutation to the Kali Yuga—thus [in the corners] starting from the northeast (īśāna). Oṃ, salutation to the lower covering, the quality of darkness (tamas); Oṃ, salutation to the middle covering, the quality of passion (rajas); Oṃ, salutation to the upper covering, the quality of goodness (sattva)—having thus worshipped the Yoga-pīṭha seat, beginning with the corpse (preta), beneath the pericarp of the lotus. Oṃ, salutation to Sadāśiva.
"Salutation to the one seated upon the great preta (mahāpreta). Thus, having meditated upon Sadāśiva— who stands above Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Rudra, who dwells within the great preta,
and who gazes upward at Śiva— and having worshipped him, one should worship both the Sakala Bhaṭṭāraka accompanied by the Goddess and the Niṣkala [Bhaṭṭāraka] above the pericarp (karṇikā).
Oṃ kṣaṃ, obeisance to the face of Īśāna; on the petal of Īśa.
Oṃ yaṃ, obeisance to the face of Tatpuruṣa; on the eastern petal. Oṃ raṃ, obeisance to the face of Aghora; on the southern petal.
Oṃ vaṃ, salutation to the face of Vāmadeva; on the northern petal. Oṃ laṃ, salutation to the face of Sadyojāta; on the western petal.
Oṃ aghorebhyaḥ sarvātmane, salutation to the heart; on the southeastern petal.
Oṃ tha ghorebhyo brahmaśirase svāhā | [To the eastern petal.
Ghoraghoratarebhyaśca jvālinyai śikhāyai vauṣaṭ | [To the chest.
Sarvataśśarvasarvebhyaḥ piṅgalāya kavacāya huṃ vāyo | [To the northwest.]

Oṃ juṃ saḥ, vaṣaṭ to the eye that has the form of light; [this is] at the center of the tip of the pericarp. Oṃ, phaṭ to the Pāśupata weapon, which is of the form of Rudra and is impenetrable; [this is] in the four directions starting from the east. Oṃ, obeisance to Vāmā; oṃ, obeisance to Jyeṣṭhā; oṃ, obeisance to Raudrī; oṃ, obeisance to Kālī; oṃ, obeisance to Kalavikariṇī; oṃ...
Salutation to Balavikariṇī. Oṃ, salutation to Balapramathinī. Oṃ, salutation to Sarvabhūtadaminī.
This group of eight deities is to be worshipped on the petals.
One should worship the power Manonmanī, white as cow’s milk, in the pericarp.
Oṃ, salutation to Manonmanī; thus, on the back of the pericarp.
Oṃ, salutation to the solar disc; on the petals.
Oṃ, homage to the moon mandala; [this is] on the filaments. Oṃ, homage to the fire mandala; [this is] on the pericarp.
In these very places:
Oṃ, salutation to Brahmā; Oṃ, salutation to Viṣṇu;
Oṃ, salutation to Rudra; Oṃ, salutation to the Great Preta-throne. This is the section on the throne. Having thus conceived the form upon it.

Right here [is] the seat and so forth for Viṣṇu. Having worshipped the deity with the six-syllabled mantra, one should request permission for the bath: "Oṃ, O Gaṇanātha, Ambikā, Svāmin, and O Sandals! Grant me, the teacher of the world, permission as I perform the sacrifice so that it may be successfully accomplished."
O Blessed One, with your permission, I shall remove the worship from this [image], which is established as your pervasive form, but I do not bestow it upon you two.
Having thus received the command,

having installed the deity upon the auspicious throne prepared with such a seat, having bathed the deity with the three weapons-mantras (astramantras), having cast the vessel for the weapon-offering (astrārghapātra) onto the throne with one [mantra], and having applied the "seat-side" (āsanapakṣa) upon the throne, one should take flowers in the hollowed palms (añjali).
Oṃ, O Blessed One, come, come! Namaḥ. Having invoked with the *āvāhana*-mudrā, [one says]:
"O Blessed One, remain, remain! Svāhā. One should cause [the deity] to stay with the *sthāpanī*-mudrā.
"O Blessed One, become completely restrained, become completely restrained! Hūṃ phaṭ! One should restrain [the deity] with the *nirodhinī*-mudrā.
"Oṃ, O Blessed One, be present, be present! Vaṣaṭ! Having thus caused [the deity] to be present with the mudrā of presence; "Oṃ hūṃ, O Blessed One, I perform the veiling;
namaḥ! Having thus veiled [the deity];
"Oṃ, O Blessed One, I render [you] nectar; namaḥ!"
Thus is the rite of immortalization (*mṛtīkaraṇa*) performed with the Amṛtamudrā.
Then, from the mantra-offering vessel (*mantrārghapātra*):
"Oṃ, Blessed One, accept the water for the feet; *namaḥ*. Oṃ, Blessed One, accept the water for sipping; *svadhā*. Oṃ, Blessed One, accept the offering (*argha*)."

Svadhā! Oṃ, Blessed One, accept this flower, vauṣaṭ! Oṃ, Blessed One, accept this incense, namaḥ! Oṃ, Blessed One, accept this lamp, namaḥ! Having thus worshipped Viṣṇu as well, one should then worship the deity with the root mantra.
One *pala* is known as the standard for a bath (*snāna*), twenty-five *palas* for an anointing (*abhyaṅga*), and one thousand *palas* is proclaimed as the great bath (*mahāsnāna*).

One should bathe [the deity] with eight *gaḍuka* measures. On special days, one should perform great baths (*mahāsnāna*) using water interspersed with milk, curd, ghee, honey, and sugarcane juice; with water containing medicinal herbs, rice, flowers, fruits, white mustard, parched grain, fragrant scents, and so forth.
One should then gradually offer the great ablutions (mahāsnāna) to Śambhu using fifteen vessels made of pure gold and jewels, filled with excellent water.

Then, intending the initiated ancestors, one should offer water with sesame seeds (tilodaka) under the lineage name of Śiva; however, for those who are uninitiated, one should offer the water with sesame seeds under one's own family lineage beneath the pedestal. Then, having worshipped the mantra-jar with the root and limb mantras—
Having bound the *mṛtamudrā* and recited the root mantra eight times, one should sprinkle the water from the principal *argha* vessel over the mantra-pot and the Lord (*īśvara*).
Then, grasping [the vessel] with both hands, [one should recite]:
*oṃ juṃ amṛte amṛte amṛteśāya pratimāṃ praviśya ghaṭikāṃ gṛhṇa 2 sānnidhyaṃ kuru 2 pañcabrahmamūrtaye*.

Having visualized [the image] as filled with nectar by means of this vidyā: "Vauṣaṭ!"—and having visualized it as filled with nectar by means of the mantra: "O Nectar! O Supreme Nectar! Having entered the image, grasp the vessel for one hour, Vauṣaṭ! Svāhā!"—one should consecrate the Blessed One.
The heart of the Bhaga is the Liṅga; the heart of the Liṅga is the Bhaga. To that Bhaga-Liṅga, indeed to Umā-Rudra, be salutation!

Thus, having touched the pedestal and the *liṅga* with the thumb and fist, there is the touching of the eyes and the body. Likewise, having touched the *sāligrāma* with the thumb and ring finger, there is the touching of the eyes and the body. Then, one should perform the expulsion with the *astra-mantra*:
"May the beings devoted to Śiva accept this offering born of the temple; whatever beings there are, and whatever spirits are their followers."
Thus.
Then, within the altar (*vedī*), one should worship the seat (*āsana*) as before:

*Oṃ ādhāraśaktaye namaḥ* (Salutation to the Support-Energy); *Oṃ anantāya namaḥ* (Salutation to Ananta); *Pṛthivyai namaḥ* (Salutation to Earth); *Surārṇavāya namaḥ* (Salutation to the Ocean of Wine); *Oṃ kandāya namaḥ* (Salutation to the Bulb). *Oṃ*...

Salutation to Nālā. Salutation to the Vidyās and Vidyeśvaras who take the form of its neck. Oṃ, salutation to the Lion Throne of Knowledge (Vidyāsiṃhāsana). Oṃ, salutation to Dharma; salutation to Jñāna; salutation to Vairāgya; salutation to Aiśvarya—in the directions beginning with the northeast. Salutation to Adharma; salutation to Ajñāna; salutation to Avairāgya; salutation to Anaiśvarya—in the directions beginning with the east. Oṃ, salutation to the Ṛgveda.
Salutation to the Yajurveda. Salutation to the Sāmaveda. Salutation to the Atharvaveda. Oṃ, salutation to the Kṛta Age. Salutation to the Tretā Age.

Salutation to the Dvāpara Age. Salutation to the Kali Age. In the intermediate directions: Oṃ, salutation to the lower covering. Salutation to the middle covering. Salutation to the upper covering. Salutation to the lotus. Salutation to the petals. Salutation to the filaments. Oṃ, salutation to the pericarp. Oṃ.
Homage to the solar disc. Homage to the lunar disc. Homage to the fiery disc. Homage to Brahmā, the lord of the solar disc.
Homage to Viṣṇu, the lord of the lunar disc. Homage to Rudra, the lord of the fiery disc. Oṃ, homage to sattva. Homage to rajas.
Salutation to Tamasī. Oṃ, salutation to Vāmā; salutation to Jyeṣṭhā; salutation to Raudrī, Kālī, Kalavikariṇī, Balavikariṇī, Balapramathinī, Sarvabhūtadamanī, and Manonmanī.
Thus [is it done] in the nine lotuses.
Then: "Salutation to the seat of the Great Preta (mahāpreta). "Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to the Form (mūrti).
Having established the deity upon that, one should offer a seat to Viṣṇu as well, in the same manner as before.

Oṃ hūṃ aghorebhyaḥ, etc., is the root mantra. Oṃ kṣaṃ, obeisance to the face of Īśāna; in the northeast corner. Oṃ yaṃ, obeisance to the face of Tatpuruṣa; in the east. Oṃ raṃ, obeisance to the face of Aghora; in the south. Oṃ vaṃ, obeisance to the face of Vāmadeva; in the north. Oṃ laṃ, obeisance to the face of Sadyojāta; in the west. Oṃ...

To the non-terrible ones, to the Self of All, to the Heart, *namaḥ*—in the southeast. Oṃ *tha*, to the terrible ones, to the Brahma-Head, *svāhā*—in the northeast. Oṃ, to those more terrible than the terrible, to the Flaming One, to the Crest (*śikhā*), *vauṣaṭ*—in the southwest. Oṃ, to all the Vasus, to the Tawny One (*piṅgala*), to the Armor (*kavaca*), *huṃ*—in the northwest. Oṃ *juṃ saḥ*, to the one whose form is light, to the Eye, *vaṣaṭ*—above the pericarp. Oṃ, salutation to you who possess the forms of Rudra, to the Impenetrable One.
*Pāśupatāstrāya phaṭ* | In all directions: *Oṃ hūṃ hrīṃ Aghoreśvari hūṃ phaṭ*. Salutation to Aghoreśvarī. The mantra of the Goddess is the root-mantra (*mūla*).
The faces are like those of the Śrīdeva.

The limbs [are worshipped] with the long [syllables] beginning with *oṃ hāṃ*. *Oṃ hūṃ namaḥ* to Niṣkala-Svacchandabhairava. The faces and limbs are as in the case of the Śrīdevī. Then one should worship the mudrās in the form of weapons: *Oṃ namaḥ* to the sword (*khaḍga*) (left); *Oṃ namaḥ* to the shield (*kheṭa*) (right); to the noose (*pāśa*) (right); to the goad (*aṅkuśa*) (left); to the arrow (*śara*) (left); to the Pināka bow (*pināka*) (right); to the boon-granting gesture (*vara*) (right); to the gesture of fearlessness (*abhaya*) (left); to the severed head (*muṇḍa*) (left); to the skull-topped staff (*khaṭvāṅga*) (right); to the lute (*vīṇā*) (right).
To the *ḍamaru* (da), to the bell (vā), to the trident (da), to the vajra (da), to the staff (vā), to the axe (da), to the mallet (vā)—Oṃ kṣmryūṃ, salutation to Kapāleśa Bhairava! [In] the east.
Oṃ hrūṃ, salutation to Śikhivāhana Bhairava! [In] the southeast.
Oṃ kṣū& namas to Bhairava, the King of Wrath; in the south. Oṃ radhrū-au& namas to Vikarāla-Bhairava; in the southwest.
Oṃ hvū-au& namas to Manmatha-Bhairava; in the west.
Oṃ hryū& namo to Meghanādabhairava; in the northwest. Oṃ hu& namo to Somarājabhairava; in the north.
Oṃ hrkṣmlvyū& namo to Vidyārājabhairava; in the northeast.
Then follows the worship of the seven enclosures (*saptāvaraṇa*). Therein, first are the Lords of Knowledge (*vidyeśvaras*):

Oṃ hrīṃ, obeisance to Ananta. Oṃ jhrūṃ, obeisance to Sūkṣma. Oṃ mūṃ, obeisance to Śivottama. Oṃ krūṃ, obeisance to Ekanetra. Oṃ kṣyāṃ, obeisance to Ekarudra. Oṃ ylūṃ, obeisance to Trimūrti. Oṃ hjūṃ, obeisance to Śrīkaṇṭha. Oṃ śīṃ...
"Salutation to Śikhaṇḍin.
Thus [is] the group of eight Vidyeśvaras in the directions starting from the east.
Oṃ rāṃ rīṃ nlūṃ, salutation to Nandin. Oṃ māṃ mīṃ mlūṃ hlauṃ, salutation to Mahākāla. Oṃ hsrāṃ, [salutation] to Bhṛṅgirudra.
Salutation! Oṃ gūṃ gāṃ, salutation to Gaṇapati. Oṃ vrāṃ, salutation to Vṛṣabha. Oṃ hsrauṃ, salutation to Kumāra. Oṃ hrīṃ saḥ, salutation to Ambikā. Oṃ hsūṃ, salutation to Caṇḍeśvara.
Thus, the eightfold Gaṇeśa [mantras] are placed in the directions starting from the east.
Thus, the lords of the world:
Oṃ lūṃ, homage to Indra, who holds a vajra in his hand; oṃ rūṃ, homage to Agni, who holds a śakti in his hand; oṃ ṅūṃ, homage to Yama, who holds a daṇḍa in his hand;
oṃ kṣūṃ, homage to Nirṛti, who holds a khaḍga in his hand; oṃ būṃ, homage to Varuṇa, who holds a pāśa in his hand; oṃ dhūṃ, homage to Vāyu.

Homage to the one with a banner in hand. Oṃ kuṃ, homage to Vīra with a mace in hand. Oṃ mūṃ, homage to Īśāna with a trident in hand. Oṃ āṃ brāṃ braṃ, homage to Brahmā with a lotus in hand. Oṃ hlāṃ, homage to Ananta with a plow in hand. These are the Lords of the World (Lokeśas).

Oṃ jmryūṃ, obeisance to Jayā. Oṃ ḍmryūṃ, obeisance to Vijayā. Oṃ gaṃ, obeisance to Subhagā. Oṃ paṃ, obeisance to Durbhagā. Oṃ msryūṃ, obeisance to Japanyā. Oṃ paṃrthahinyai, obeisance to [Paṃrthahinī]. Oṃ hsryūṃ, obeisance to Aparājitā. Oṃ rāṃ, obeisance to Karālī. Thus are the Mothers (Mātaraḥ).
Then, with the root mantra: *namaḥ* to the Sun;

*oṃ srūṃ*, *namaḥ* to the Moon; *oṃ rhrūṃ*, *namaḥ* to Mars; *oṃ shryūṃ*, *namaḥ* to Mercury; *oṃ rsūṃ*, *namaḥ* to Jupiter; *oṃ hrīṃ*, *namaḥ* to Venus; *oṃ rkṣmryūṃ*, *namaḥ* to Saturn; *oṃ dhūṃ*, *namaḥ* to Rāhu; *oṃ hrīṃ*, *namaḥ* to Ketu.
Homage! Thus are the planets.

Oṃ, homage to Ananta, the king of nāgas. Oṃ, homage to Vāsuki, the king of nāgas. Likewise [homage to] Padma, Mahāpadma, Takṣaka, Kārkoṭaka, Śaṅkhapāla, and Kulika, the nāga. Thus is the group of eight nāga kings.

Oṃ vajrāya phaṭ | Oṃ śaktaye phaṭ | To the staff (daṇḍa), to the sword (khaḍga), to the noose (pāśa), to the banner (dhvaja), to the mace (gadā), to the trident (triśūla), to the lotus (padma), to the plow (hala) phaṭ. Thus is the enclosure of the vajra and so forth.
Thus is the worship of the seven enclosures.
Then follows the joining of the channels.

Having meditated on the power (śakti) arisen from one’s own locus of action (karmasthāna), which has extended as far as the *dvādaśānta*, and having taken the nectar (amṛta) from that place— [the power] having emerged through the nostril at the *dvādaśānta* via the left nostril, having entered the right nostril of the deity,
having reached his locus of action, having arisen from there, and having reached his *dvādaśānta*— and having taken the nectar from that [place].

One should contemplate that [fecal matter] exiting through the left nostril, having spread as a single channel through all the coverings (*āvaraṇa*), and then entering one's own self again through the right nostril. This is the joining of the channels (*nāḍī-sandhāna*).
Following that is the process of unification (*paramīkaraṇa*): having meditated on the Power (*śakti*) arisen from the locus of action within oneself, as it has emerged through the *dvādaśānta*.
One should meditate upon [the goddess] who has entered simultaneously into all the coverings (*āvaraṇas*), remaining in an uninterrupted flow at the *dvādaśānta*, and merged into one's own self.

Having thus performed the worship up to the point of the unification of mantras for the water for the feet, the water for sipping, and the offering (*arghya*), as well as the unification of the channels (*nāḍī*) and the process of supreme transformation (*paramīkaraṇa*);

thereafter, having performed an extensive worship, one should perform the recitation (*japa*) of the root mantra according to one's capacity. For the faces and the limbs, the recitation should be one-tenth [of the root].
O You who protect the most secret of secrets, accept this recitation performed by us; O Lord, may accomplishment be mine through Your grace, while You remain as my witness.
Thus ends the offering of the recitation (*japa-nivedana*).
Then, having sprinkled [the substance] from the *argha* vessel and rendered it nectar-like with the *amṛta-mudrā*:
Oṃ saḥ! To the nectar-born Soma, svāhā! O you who possess the nature of the ritual substance, ṭhaḥ ṭhaḥ!
Divine nectar was produced before the churning of the ocean of milk; may this food, in the form of nectar, be accepted as an offering.
Having thus recollected the root mantra and offered the food offering (naivedya),
one should perform the worship of the Lord of the Field (kṣetreśa).

Oṃ hrāṃ kṣaṃ kṣūṃ, homage to Heruka! [In] the east. Oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ lāṃ kṣeṃ kṣīṃ, homage to Tripurāntaka! [In] the southeast. Oṃ hrīṃ hūṃ kṣīṃ, homage to Agnivetāla! [In] the south. Aiṃ hrīṃ kṣūṃ hūṃ, homage to Agnijihva! [In] the southwest. Oṃ hrīṃ hrīṃ hūṃ, homage to Kurpara! [In] the west. Homage to Kāla! [In] the northwest. Oṃ kṣā yūṃ kṣīṃ.

Salutation to Karālin. In the north: Oṃ āṃ yūṃ kṣmīṃ, salutation to Ekapāda. In the northeast: Oṃ kṣūṃ yūṃ kṣāṃ, salutation to Bhīmarūpa. In the center: Salutation to Ūrdhva-Ḍāmara. Below: Salutation to Hāṭakeśvara.
Now, the dismissal:
"O Lord, grant me permission to consume this food offering; O Supreme Lord, forgive me for the sake of accomplishing the maintenance of my body."
Oṃ hūṃ, O Blessed One, forgive me! Hūṃ phaṭ! Hūṃ, O Blessed Lady, forgive me! Hūṃ phaṭ!
Whatever we have done, O God, whether always well-done or ill-done—O Śaṅkara, for me who abide in the state of Śiva, destroy it! Hūṃ haḥ!

*Kṣaḥ kṣaḥ kṣapaya śaṅkara*—this is also a reading. "O Lord, please forgive us for this much; you have been troubled. This is the mantra of forgiveness (*kṣānti-mantra*). Having arisen in the form of a flame, one should meditate upon the Supreme Soul of Fire as being perfectly tranquil, and with hymns of praise, one should bow with devotion to Śiva who is well-pleased.
Forgive whatever I have done that is deficient or excessive, O you whose form is the universe; be gracious, O Lord of Gods, salutations be unto you! Depart satisfied for the sake of returning again.
Whatever has occurred that was devoid of materials, devoid of ritual action, or devoid of mantra—may all that reach fulfillment through your grace, O Maheśvara.

Then, having meditated upon the worshipped mantras as being absorbed into the Lord, shining with the brilliance of sparks of fire, one should contemplate that Lord in the form of a flame residing within the heart. Thus it is auspicious. Then follows the *samayā*.
After that, one should take up the vessel of offering (*arghapātra*). Then: "O Karālinī, [place] that in the one called Kāla; that in the tongue of Agni; that in Agni."

[He is] in the Vetāla; [He is] in the destroyer of Tripura; [He is] in the crusher; [He is] in the mallet; [He is] in the axe; [He is] in the staff; [He is] in the thunderbolt; [He is] in the trident; [He is] in that bell; [She is] in the hand-drum; [He is] in the lute; [She is] in the skull-topped staff; [He is] in the skull-cup; [He is] in the gesture of fearlessness, [granting] fearlessness and boons; [He is] in the Pināka bow, [granting] boons; [He is] in the Pināka; [He is] in the arrow; [He is] in the goad; [He is] in the goad; [He is] in the noose; [He is] in the shield; [He is] in the sword; [He is] in the sword; [He is] in Īśāna.
One should contemplate him as merged in Kuvīra, in Vāyu, in Varuṇa, in Nairṛta, in Yama, in Agni, in Indra,
in Indrarājabhairava, in Somarājabhairava, in Meghanādabhairava, in Manmathabhairava, in Vikarālabhairava,
in Krodharājabhairava, and in Śikhivāhanabhairava. One should contemplate him as dissolved in Kapāleśabhairava.

As before, one should contemplate Kapāleśa-Bhairava as dissolved in Āmardaka; Āmardaka in Śakti; Śakti in Astra; Astra in Netra; Netra in Kavaca; Kavaca in Śikhā; Śikhā in Śiva; the head in the region of the heart; the heart in Sadyojāta; Sadyojāta in Vāmadeva; Vāmadeva in Aghora; that [Aghora] in Tatpuruṣa; that [Tatpuruṣa] in Īśāna; that [Īśāna] in the Lord with parts (sakala-bhaṭṭāraka); and that [Lord] in the Lord of Mantras without parts (niṣkala-mantrīśvara).

[One should place] that [libation] in the *argha* vessel; one should contemplate the *argha* vessel as dissolved into one's own self. Having worshipped Bhairava with the ritual procedure taught in the venerable *Svacchanda-tantra*, may the wise attain identification with Him for the sake of the perpetual accomplishment of absolute sovereignty. The wretchedness of worldly existence dissolves, the glory of liberation takes refuge in the heart-lotus, and it shines forth.
Supreme bliss spreads wherever that worship of the Lord prevails. May this *Svacchanda-patrikā* also reach completion;
may it be for the pleasure of the venerable Bhairava, who is one's own Self. May there be auspiciousness!
Now, the intermediate time.
She should be worshipped according to the convention in order to prevent the violation of the prescribed rule.

Oṃ juṃ saḥ! To the Lord of Nectar, whose form is nectar, the inner self of all beings, whose body is the great void—ward off the violation of all commitments (samaya), fulfill the commitment! To the one whose mantra-body is common to all—hrīṃ svāhā! Oṃ hrīṃ! O Nectar, supreme nectar, eternal! Klīṃ saḥ! O Mistress of Nectar, who dwells within all beings, whose nature is Brahman, whose body is the great void—ward off the violation of all commitments; [fulfill] every commitment.

Fill [me] for the sake of the glory of immortality, svāhā! Oṃ hūṃ, to the one whose essential nature is peaceful knowledge, hāṃ hīṃ hūṃ haiṃ hauṃ haḥ, to the one who wards off the violation of all commitments, hrīṃ svāhā! Thus ends the *Svacchanda-samaya*. Oṃ, O Aghora, juṃ, O Ghora, saḥ, O most terrible of the terrible! Hrīṃ, O Śarva, O All-pervading One! Hūṃ, salutations to you in the form of Rudra; to the Weapon, phaṭ! Oṃ, O Aghora, the Self of All, to the Heart, namaḥ! Oṃ...

*Juṃ tha ghore brahmaśisare svāhā*. *Saḥ ghoraghoratare jvāliniśikhāyai vauṣaṭ*. *Oṃ hrīṃ sarvataḥ śarvasarve piṅgalāya kavacāya huṃ hūṃ namaste rudrarūpe durbhedyāya pāśupatāstrāya phaṭ*. This is the *utkīlana-vidyā*, the ritual for the unbolting of Aghora.

Oṃ aghore aiṃ tha ghore hrīṃ ghoraghoratare śrīṃ sarvataḥ sarvasarve | phreṃ rudrarūpe hsphreṃ namaste | The mantra accompanied by the syllable *bhakāra* is situated in the middle; [if] the eight *kīlas* are not applied, it will not be accomplished.
In all these tantras, that which is devoid of vigor is revealed—devoid of the individual soul and vital breath, and abandoned by the five seed-syllables.
